name: upgrade_pydantic_allow_mutation_to_frozen_configdict
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x class Config: allow_mutation=False to 2.x model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True) - the v1 key is silently ignored (just a warning) under pydantic 2.x, so an unmigrated model stays fully mutable; incomplete-fix broken switches to the ConfigDict container but keeps the stale allow_mutation key name, which v2 still does not recognize
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). Point in point.py uses the pydantic 1.x `class Config: allow_mutation = False` pattern to make instances immutable after construction. Under the installed pydantic 2.x, the `allow_mutation` config key has been REMOVED - it is silently ignored (with only a warning), so Point instances are actually still fully mutable, defeating the original intent. Migrate to the pydantic 2.x pattern: `model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)` as a class attribute. After the fix, assigning to an existing field on a Point instance must raise an error instead of silently succeeding.

test_setup_files.test_point.py:
from point import Point

p = Point(x=1, y=2)
assert p.x == 1 and p.y == 2

try:
    p.x = 99
    raise AssertionError("expected mutation to be rejected on a frozen model")
except AssertionError:
    raise
except Exception:
    pass

assert p.x == 1, f"x should be unchanged after the rejected mutation, got {p.x}"

print("PASS")

reference_solution.point.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Point(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    x: int
    y: int

files.point.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Point(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(allow_mutation=False)

    x: int
    y: int
